They saw my Shardless Agent pull at the threads of reality, and for a moment, they glimpsed the *Living End*—only for me to snatch it away! Why would I trade my glorious, living army for the dust of the graveyard when victory was already within my grasp?

With a single command, my minions—the Generous Ents, the Overlord of the Balemurk, even the lowly Street Wraith—surged forward in a final, devastating onslaught. 44 power! A cacophony of destruction that their "six permanents" could never hope to contain!

**MWAHAHAHAHAHA!** 

As the last of their life force flickers out, let them remember this: I am the architect of their downfall, and every card played was but a step toward their inevitable erasure! The world is mine! 

**Victory is mine!**

gameOver.message: Player Gem3F Villain is the winner

annotations.description: In a hand with no lands, Tormod's Crypt is a free artifact that helps enable Mox Opal's metalcraft (Mox Opal + Mishra's Bauble + Tormod's Crypt = 3 artifacts = metalcraft active). Metallic Rebuke is a reactive counterspell that requires blue mana and is much harder to leverage without lands. Bottoming the free artifact reduces metalcraft reliability.
annotations.actionTaken: Bottomed Tormod's Crypt, keeping Metallic Rebuke
annotations.betterLine: Bottom Metallic Rebuke instead, keeping all cheap artifacts to maximize chances of enabling Mox Opal's metalcraft in a landless hand

annotations.description: With no lands in hand, the player needs to enable Metalcraft (3 artifacts) to activate Mox Opal for mana. The correct sequence is to cast Mox Opal first, then Mishra's Bauble, then Engineered Explosives (for X=0) to reach Metalcraft and have access to mana. By casting Mishra's Bauble first, nothing changes functionally since all three zero-cost artifacts will be cast this turn anyway, BUT casting Mox Opal first is strictly better because if the opponent has any instant-speed interaction (e.g., a response that would prevent further casting), you want your mana source on the battlefield first. Additionally, casting Mishra's Bauble first and sacrificing it won't draw a card until next upkeep, so it doesn't help find a land this turn. The order matters slightly - Mox Opal should come down first as a general sequencing principle of deploying mana sources before other spells. However, since all three will likely resolve this turn with no opponent interaction possible (it's the main phase and opponent has no board), the practical impact is minimal.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Mishra's Bauble first before Mox Opal
annotations.betterLine: Cast Mox Opal first, then Mishra's Bauble, then Engineered Explosives for X=0 to enable Metalcraft immediately and have mana available as early as possible

annotations.description: The player passed priority without casting Mox Opal or activating Mishra's Bauble. Mox Opal costs 0 and should be deployed to build toward metalcraft (currently only Mishra's Bauble as an artifact). Additionally, Mishra's Bauble should be activated to sacrifice it and look at the opponent's top card while drawing a card next upkeep - it's a free ability with no downside. The player's reasoning about 'the Bauble spell is on the stack' appears confused since Mishra's Bauble is already on the battlefield, not on the stack. At minimum, casting Mox Opal for free advances the artifact count toward metalcraft and enables Metallic Rebuke via improvise.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting any spells or activating abilities.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Mox Opal (free), then activate Mishra's Bauble targeting opponent to get information and a delayed draw. This builds toward metalcraft (would have 2 artifacts) and gets value from Bauble before the turn passes.

annotations.description: The player declined to activate Mishra's Bauble, which is a free ability that sacrifices the Bauble to look at the top card of the opponent's library and draw a card next upkeep. There is no reason not to activate it - it provides free information and a free card. The player's reasoning about 'letting the Bauble effect happen' suggests confusion, as Mishra's Bauble requires an active tap-sacrifice activation. Additionally, casting Engineered Explosives for X=0 (using no colored mana) would give a third artifact for Mox Opal's Metalcraft, but the player also declined that. At minimum, activating Bauble is pure upside with no downside.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without activating Mishra's Bauble or casting any spells.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Mishra's Bauble targeting the opponent to get information and draw a card next upkeep. Could also consider casting Engineered Explosives for X=0 first to enable Metalcraft on Mox Opal before activating Bauble, though that uses the Explosives. At the very least, activating Bauble is free value that should not be declined.

annotations.description: Targeting yourself with Mishra's Bauble is almost always worse than targeting your opponent. Looking at your own top card gives you marginal information (you'll draw it next turn regardless), while looking at the opponent's top card gives you valuable information about what they're planning, which is especially useful when you're holding Metallic Rebuke as a counterspell. Knowing what the opponent will draw helps you decide whether to hold up countermagic or deploy threats.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted themselves with Mishra's Bauble to look at their own top card.
annotations.betterLine: Target the opponent (Gem3F Villain) with Mishra's Bauble to see their top card, gaining information about their next draw to better plan counterspell usage with Metallic Rebuke.

annotations.description: The player cast Engineered Explosives seemingly intending to destroy Hedge Maze, but Engineered Explosives only destroys nonland permanents. Hedge Maze is a land and cannot be destroyed by EE. Additionally, casting EE for X=0 wastes a card since the opponent has no nonland permanents with mana value 0 on the battlefield. The player also had Mishra's Bauble in the graveyard, not on the battlefield, so metalcraft was NOT active (only Mox Opal + Spirebluff Canal = 1 artifact), meaning Mox Opal couldn't tap for mana anyway. Even if metalcraft were active, EE cannot hit lands. The better play would have been to cast Shadowspear (1 mana) to get a third artifact on the battlefield for metalcraft, or cast Pinnacle Emissary for its warp cost to start developing threats.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Engineered Explosives for X=0, apparently trying to destroy Hedge Maze (a land)
annotations.betterLine: Cast Shadowspear for {1} using Spirebluff Canal to enable metalcraft (Mox Opal + Shadowspear + Spirebluff Canal = 2 artifacts, still not enough — actually Mox Opal is 1 artifact, so Shadowspear would make 2). Better yet, cast Pinnacle Emissary for its warp cost {U/R} to develop a 3/3 threat and start generating value, or play Shadowspear to work toward metalcraft and save EE for when the opponent actually deploys nonland threats.

annotations.description: With 4 artifacts on board (Mox Opal, Engineered Explosives, Shadowspear, and the tapped Spirebluff Canal is a land not artifact), Mox Opal has Metalcraft active (Mox Opal, Engineered Explosives, Shadowspear = 3 artifacts). Casting Pinnacle Emissary for its Warp cost of {U/R} would only cost 1 mana, deploying a 3/3 that generates tokens when artifact spells are cast. It would exile at end step but could be recast later. However, the player has Metallic Rebuke in hand and the opponent has only 1 tapped land, so holding up countermagic isn't critical this turn. Warping out Pinnacle Emissary for just 1 mana while still having mana available for Rebuke (with Improvise from artifacts) could have been a strong tempo play - getting a 3/3 attacker and setting up future recasts from exile.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without casting anything, keeping mana open with no pressing need for countermagic against an opponent with only 1 tapped land.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Pinnacle Emissary for its Warp cost ({U/R}) using Mox Opal. This deploys a 3/3 threat that will exile at end step but can be recast later, while still potentially leaving mana for Metallic Rebuke via Improvise if needed on opponent's turn.

annotations.description: Casting Pinnacle Emissary for its warp cost (U/R) on turn 2 means it will be exiled at the beginning of the next end step, giving only a temporary 3/3 body. While the opponent's board is empty, this doesn't apply meaningful pressure since the creature leaves at end of turn. More importantly, deploying this now leaves only Metallic Rebuke (with improvise) as interaction, but tapping Mox Opal for the warp cost may constrain mana. The player could instead hold up Metallic Rebuke to counter whatever the opponent plays on turn 3, which is likely more impactful against decks running threats like Overlord of the Balemurk. The Emissary can be warped on a later turn when there's more mana available to both deploy threats and hold up countermagic.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Pinnacle Emissary for its warp cost, creating a temporary 3/3 that gets exiled at end step.
annotations.betterLine: Pass the turn holding up Metallic Rebuke (castable for U with improvise from 3 artifacts) to counter the opponent's next play, then deploy Pinnacle Emissary on a future turn when the tempo is more valuable or when you can recast it from exile alongside other plays.

annotations.description: Pinnacle Emissary was cast for its Warp cost ({U/R}), meaning it would exile itself at the beginning of the next end step anyway and only be on the battlefield temporarily. Using Subtlety's evoke (which costs exiling Shardless Agent, one of the best cards in hand with cascade value) to bounce a creature that was going to leave play on its own is a very poor trade of resources - essentially 2 cards for a minimal tempo gain against a temporary threat.
annotations.actionTaken: Evoked Subtlety by exiling Shardless Agent to bounce the Warped Pinnacle Emissary back to library.
annotations.betterLine: Let Pinnacle Emissary resolve. It would exile itself at end step due to Warp. Save Subtlety and Shardless Agent for more impactful threats. The 3/3 body for one turn and potential token generation from a few artifacts is far less costly than losing two premium cards.

annotations.description: Kimi25 has a 3/3 Pinnacle Emissary on board against an opponent with no creatures and only tapped lands. The opponent is at 20 life. Skipping the attack phase means missing 3 free damage. There's no reason not to attack here - the opponent has no blockers and no untapped mana for tricks. Additionally, equipping Shadowspear first (using 2 mana) would give the Emissary +1/+1, trample, and lifelink, allowing a 4-damage attack with lifegain. Even without equipping, attacking for 3 is strictly better than not attacking.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority and skipped the attack phase entirely, dealing 0 damage.
annotations.betterLine: Equip Shadowspear to Pinnacle Emissary for {2}, then attack for 4 with trample and lifelink (going to 22 life, opponent to 16). At minimum, attack with the unequipped 3/3 for 3 damage.

annotations.description: Overlord of the Balemurk is a 5/5 that mills four cards on ETB and returns a creature or planeswalker from graveyard to hand. Against a Living End deck with Street Wraith, Subtlety, Endurance, and Generous Ent already in the graveyard, this is devastating — it will mill more creatures into the graveyard (fueling a future Living End) and immediately recur a powerful creature like Endurance or Subtlety. The opponent cast it for its full cost ({3}{B}{B}), meaning it enters as a 5/5 creature. With Metallic Rebuke available and Improvise making it cost only {U} (tap Engineered Explosives and Shadowspear as artifacts, plus Steam Vents or Spirebluff Canal for {U}), this was a free counter that should have been used on a must-answer threat. The opponent would need to pay {3} to avoid the counter, which on turn 3 with all lands tapped they cannot do.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to cast Metallic Rebuke, allowing Overlord of the Balemurk to resolve.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Metallic Rebuke targeting Overlord of the Balemurk, using Improvise (tap Engineered Explosives and Shadowspear) plus one blue mana from Steam Vents or Spirebluff Canal. The opponent has no mana available to pay {3}, so it would be a hard counter on a major threat.

annotations.description: The Overlord of the Balemurk trigger lets you return a non-Avatar creature or planeswalker from graveyard to hand. The player chose Endurance over other options. While Endurance is a powerful card with flash, in this context the player is on a Living End deck with Street Wraith, Subtlety, Endurance, and Generous Ent in the graveyard. Returning Endurance to hand means it won't be reanimated by Living End, AND if cast, Endurance's ETB would shuffle graveyard cards into library - which is anti-synergistic with Living End's game plan of having creatures in the graveyard to reanimate. Street Wraith could be returned and cycled again to draw a card and put it back in the graveyard for Living End. Generous Ent could be returned and forestcycled to fix mana while going back to graveyard. Subtlety provides interaction against opponent's spells. Endurance seems like the worst choice here since it actively works against the Living End strategy.
annotations.actionTaken: Returned Endurance from graveyard to hand via Overlord of the Balemurk trigger.
annotations.betterLine: Return Street Wraith to hand (can cycle it again for a card draw while putting it back in graveyard for Living End), or Subtlety (provides flash interaction against opponent's threats without conflicting with Living End plan).

annotations.description: Suspending Living End telegraphs the board wipe 3 turns in advance, giving the opponent time to prepare (hold up Metallic Rebuke, stop committing creatures, etc.). More importantly, in a Living End cascade deck, Living End should be cascaded into via Shardless Agent, not suspended. Suspending it removes it from the library where cascade spells could find it. Formidable Speaker could have been cast to discard a card and tutor for a cascade creature (like another Shardless Agent) to cast Living End immediately or next turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Suspended Living End, telegraphing the plan and removing it from the cascade pool.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Formidable Speaker (3 mana), discard Wistfulness or another card to search for Shardless Agent or another cascade creature, then cascade into Living End on a future turn without telegraphing it. Alternatively, just deploy Formidable Speaker as a body while keeping Living End in the library for cascade.

annotations.description: The player activated Shadowspear's {1} ability (which removes hexproof and indestructible from opponents' permanents) but their reasoning says they wanted to equip Shadowspear to Pinnacle Emissary. These are two completely different abilities. The {1} activated ability is not the equip ability - it just strips hexproof/indestructible from opponent's permanents until end of turn, which is pointless here since the opponent has no hexproof or indestructible permanents. The Overlord of the Balemurk (as an enchantment with impending, not yet a creature) has neither keyword. This wastes 1 mana for no benefit. The player should have either equipped Shadowspear (costs {2}) to Pinnacle Emissary before combat, or simply moved to combat without activating anything.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Shadowspear's {1} ability to remove hexproof and indestructible from opponent's permanents, which had neither keyword.
annotations.betterLine: Either equip Shadowspear to Pinnacle Emissary for {2} before combat to gain +1/+1, trample, and lifelink, or save the mana and proceed to combat directly, keeping mana open for Metallic Rebuke.

annotations.description: The Drone Token (1/1 flying) could have attacked for free since the opponent has no creatures (Overlord is still an enchantment with time counters) and all opponent lands are tapped, meaning no interaction possible. Missing 1 free damage.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Pinnacle Emissary, leaving the Drone Token back.
annotations.betterLine: Select 'All attack' to also send the Drone Token for an additional 1 damage with zero risk, dealing 5 total instead of 4.

annotations.description: Gem3F Villain had 6 lands capable of producing the necessary GGUU to cast Wistfulness with both modes active (exile an artifact/enchantment + draw 2 cards), which would have been significantly more impactful than Formidable Speaker. Wistfulness could exile Shadowspear or Engineered Explosives while drawing 2 cards and providing a 6/5 body.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Formidable Speaker, a 2/4 for 3 mana that requires discarding to tutor
annotations.betterLine: Cast Wistfulness for {3}{G/U}{G/U} spending both GG and UU to exile an opponent's artifact/enchantment (Shadowspear or Engineered Explosives) and draw 2 cards, getting a 6/5 body with much greater board impact and card advantage

annotations.description: Formidable Speaker is a key creature that, when it enters, allows the opponent to discard a card to tutor for any creature. Given the opponent's graveyard-focused strategy with Overlord of the Balemurk and various recursion tools, letting them resolve a creature tutor is very dangerous - they could find Endurance, another Overlord, or any silver bullet creature. The analyst has Metallic Rebuke in hand and sufficient artifacts to cast it with Improvise (Engineered Explosives, Shadowspear, and the untapped Spirebluff Canal for U, plus tapping two artifacts for Improvise covers the {2}{U} cost). The opponent would need to pay {3} to force the spell through, which with 6 lands is possible but still costs them significant mana.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority and let Formidable Speaker resolve without countering it.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Metallic Rebuke targeting Formidable Speaker, using the untapped Spirebluff Canal for {U} and tapping Engineered Explosives and Shadowspear for Improvise to cover the {2}. Even if the opponent pays {3}, that's a significant tempo cost. If they can't pay, you deny them a creature tutor which could find a game-winning threat.

annotations.description: Gem3F Villain passed without casting anything despite having the option to evoke Wistfulness for {G/U}{G/U} (2 mana from untapped lands) to exile an opponent's artifact like Engineered Explosives (which threatens their board including Overlord of the Balemurk with impending counters) or Shadowspear. At 12 life facing a Pinnacle Emissary, removing a key artifact could be valuable.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without casting any spells during precombat main phase.
annotations.betterLine: Evoke Wistfulness for GG to exile Engineered Explosives, protecting their board from a potential sweeper, or exile Shadowspear to reduce the opponent's combat effectiveness.

annotations.description: Wistfulness is being cast (likely for its evoke cost based on the trigger). If it was cast with {U}{U} spent, it draws two cards and discards one, giving the opponent significant card advantage. If cast with {G}{G}, it exiles an artifact or enchantment the opponent controls - potentially targeting Engineered Explosives, Shadowspear, Mox Opal, or even the Drone Token. Either mode represents a meaningful threat that should be countered. The player had Metallic Rebuke available with improvise potential (untapped Engineered Explosives, Shadowspear, Spirebluff Canal, and Drone Token could help pay costs), making it castable. Letting Wistfulness resolve gives the opponent either card advantage or permanent destruction for free.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to counter Wistfulness with Metallic Rebuke, allowing it to resolve.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Metallic Rebuke targeting Wistfulness. With improvise from untapped artifacts (Engineered Explosives, Shadowspear) plus the untapped Spirebluff Canal, the mana cost is easily payable. Countering Wistfulness denies the opponent either card advantage or artifact/enchantment removal, and since it was evoked, the opponent also loses the card entirely.

annotations.description: Declined to equip Lavaspur Boots or Shadowspear to Pinnacle Emissary before combat, despite the opponent being completely tapped out. Equipping Shadowspear (2 mana) would give +1/+1, trample, and lifelink, allowing Pinnacle Emissary to attack as a 4/4 trampler with lifelink past Formidable Speaker (2/4). Even Lavaspur Boots (1 mana) would add +1/+0 and ward {1} for protection. They still had plenty of mana/artifacts to hold up Metallic Rebuke via improvise.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed on all equipment activations in precombat main phase
annotations.betterLine: Equip Shadowspear to Pinnacle Emissary for 2 mana, making it a 4/4 with trample and lifelink, then attack. Still can hold up Metallic Rebuke with remaining mana and improvise.

annotations.description: The opponent is at 12 life with all lands tapped and only Formidable Speaker (2/4, no flying) and Overlord of the Balemurk (5/5) as potential blockers. Pinnacle Emissary is a 4/3 (likely pumped by Shadowspear or counters from artifact ETBs). The Drone Token has flying so it can't be blocked by ground creatures. If both attack, Overlord could block the Emissary (trading 4/3 into 5/5, Emissary dies) or Formidable Speaker could block (2/4 blocks 4/3, Speaker dies). But the opponent's lands are all tapped, meaning no combat tricks. Attacking with both forces the opponent to make unfavorable blocks - if they block Emissary with the 5/5, the Drone still gets through for 1 (total 1 damage but Emissary is preserved if they don't block it). Actually, if all lands are tapped, the opponent can't activate Formidable Speaker's untap ability either. Attacking with both means: opponent blocks Emissary with Overlord 5/5 (Emissary dies, Overlord lives) and Drone gets 1 through, or blocks Emissary with Speaker 2/4 (Speaker dies, Emissary lives) and Drone gets 1 through, or doesn't block at all (5 damage total). The best case is 5 damage (opponent to 7), worst case is losing Emissary but dealing 1. Given the opponent has all lands tapped, attacking with both is better - the Emissary likely survives since opponent probably blocks with Speaker to save Overlord, and you deal 5 damage instead of 1. Only attacking with the Drone for 1 damage is overly conservative and misses 4 potential damage.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only the 1/1 Drone Token for 1 damage.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with both Pinnacle Emissary and Drone Token. With all opponent lands tapped, opponent must make unfavorable blocking decisions. If unblocked, deal 5 damage (opponent to 7). If Emissary is blocked by Speaker 2/4, Speaker dies and you still deal 1 with Drone. This is significantly more pressure.

annotations.description: Kimi25 chose to attack with only Pinnacle Emissary (a 4/3 with the Drone Token also available as a 1/1 flyer). The opponent is at 12 life with all lands tapped and only Formidable Speaker (2/4) and Overlord of the Balemurk (5/5) as potential blockers. The Drone Token has flying and likely cannot be blocked by either ground creature (Overlord is 5/5 without flying, Formidable Speaker is 2/4 without flying). Attacking with both Pinnacle Emissary and the Drone Token would deal an additional 1 damage for free. There's essentially no downside to sending the Drone Token as well since it has flying and the opponent has no flyers on board.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Pinnacle Emissary (4/3), leaving the Drone Token back.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with both Pinnacle Emissary and the Drone Token to deal 1 extra unblockable flying damage, putting the opponent to 11 (or lower depending on blocks).

annotations.description: Metallic Rebuke was used to counter Shardless Agent, but in standard Magic rules, cascade triggers on cast and resolves before the original spell. By the time priority is available to counter the Agent, the cascade trigger has likely already resolved, meaning the counter only stops the 2/2 body. Using Metallic Rebuke on a 2/2 body is a poor use of the counterspell, especially when holding Kappa Cannoneer that needs protection from removal. The player's reasoning incorrectly assumes countering stops cascade.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Metallic Rebuke to counter Shardless Agent, believing it would prevent cascade
annotations.betterLine: Let Shardless Agent resolve (the 2/2 is not a significant threat) and save Metallic Rebuke to protect Kappa Cannoneer when deploying it, or to counter a more impactful spell from the opponent

annotations.description: By stacking Overlord of the Balemurk to resolve last (after Formidable Speaker), they miss the opportunity to mill 4 cards first, which could provide better information and a returned creature card before deciding what to discard to Formidable Speaker's tutor ability. Resolving Overlord first would let them see what gets milled, return a creature to hand, and then have more discard options for the tutor.
annotations.actionTaken: Ordered triggers so Formidable Speaker resolves first (discard Endurance to tutor), then Generous Ent, then Overlord of the Balemurk last.
annotations.betterLine: Order triggers so Overlord of the Balemurk resolves first (mill 4, return a creature), then Formidable Speaker (discard with more information and options), then Generous Ent.

annotations.description: Engineered Explosives has 0 charge counters, so activating it destroys all nonland permanents with MV 0. This destroys their own Mox Opal while hitting nothing on the opponent's side. This wastes two artifacts (EE sacrificed as cost + Mox Opal destroyed) for no benefit, reducing their artifact count for affinity/improvise/metalcraft.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Engineered Explosives (0 counters) to destroy all MV-0 nonland permanents, destroying their own Mox Opal for no gain.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Emry for {U} (affinity reducing cost with 4 artifacts), then use remaining mana and artifacts to cast Kappa Cannoneer via improvise, developing the board with real threats instead of destroying own resources.

annotations.description: At 9 life with 2 untapped lands and Food tokens about to be destroyed by Engineered Explosives (0 counters), Gem3F passed without sacrificing a Food token for 3 life. The Food tokens were destroyed for no benefit when at least one could have been cashed in for 3 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating any Food tokens, allowing all three to be destroyed by Engineered Explosives.
annotations.betterLine: Sacrifice one Food token for 3 life using the 2 available mana (Underground Mortuary + Breeding Pool), going from 9 to 12 life before the tokens are destroyed anyway.

annotations.description: Gem3F Villain had Endurance (flash) in hand and could have cast it targeting Kimi25 Analyst before Living End resolved. This would have put all of Kimi25's graveyard (including Pinnacle Emissary, Arcbound Ravager, Aether Spellbomb, etc.) on the bottom of their library, so when Living End resolves, the opponent gets back zero creatures while Gem3F gets back all their graveyard creatures. Instead, by passing, Living End will return creatures to both sides.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting Endurance, allowing Living End to resolve with the opponent's graveyard intact.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Endurance targeting Kimi25 Analyst to empty their graveyard before Living End resolves, ensuring a massively one-sided Living End that only returns Gem3F's creatures.

annotations.description: Villain declined to cast Endurance (flash, 3/4 reach) while the opponent has Emry on the battlefield with a graveyard full of powerful artifacts (Mox Opal, Arcbound Ravager, Engineered Explosives, Aether Spellbomb, etc.).
